finding: Components held in table cells skip the component schema, so a malformed cell crashes check with no JSON answer.
why: A cell only needs `type`; `children`, `style` and `id` are never type-checked, so `children: "oops"` reaches registry.validate (registry.py:65, :78) as a string and raises TypeError, outside the Refusal catch in engine.main (inferred by reading, not run); this breaks the one-JSON-object and 'refuses and names item and field' acceptance bullets.
fix: Check each nested component against the document `component` shape (additionalProperties false, children list, style/id string) in registry.validate before recursing, and add a negative test for a malformed cell.
evidence: "items": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "object", "required": ["type"]}]}; registry.py:65 `return component.get("children") or []`; engine.py:303-309 catches only Refusal

finding: describe() crashes on a non-object map entry, so check prints a traceback instead of a refusal.
why: Input {"maps": ["abc"]} gives schema problem path ("maps", 0); line 70 sets entry = "abc" and line 71 calls (entry or {}).get('id'), which raises AttributeError; main catches only Refusal, so there is no JSON object and no exit 1.
fix: Test isinstance(entry, dict) before .get, as the rounds branch does.
evidence: entry = (doc.get("maps") or [None])[path[1]]  /  name = f"map {(entry or {}).get('id') or path[1]}"

finding: Components held in props (table cells) never pass the component-shell schema, so check accepts bad cells and check or render crashes.
why: validate() checks a held component only against its type's props schema; the table cell schema is {"type":"object","required":["type"]}. A cell {"type":"chip","props":{...},"id":5} or "style":5 passes check, then html.escape(5) raises in render_component; "children":"ab" makes _held iterate characters and validate() raise TypeError; "type":["x"] is unhashable in lookup(). Extra keys are kept silently, so additionalProperties:false is not enforced for cells.
fix: In validate(), run problems() with the $defs/component schema on every held component before the type check.
evidence: base_table.py:38 "items": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "object", "required": ["type"]}]}; registry.py:95 for sub, child in _held(component, kind): found += validate(child, ...)

finding: Possible leak: page-assembly types `card` and `round-banner` are public registry names that take loose props.
why: An agent-written body of type `card` passes check because `item` only requires id, kind, body; render then hits `KIND_WORDS[item["kind"]]` (base_card.py:84) and raises KeyError with no JSON answer; the unknown-type message (registry.py:82) also lists these internal names as valid.
fix: Mark engine-owned types as internal (refused in agent documents) or validate `item` fully in the card schema.
evidence: register_component("card", {... "properties": {"item": {"type": "object", "required": ["id", "kind", "body"]}, ...}}, render_card)

finding: The saved-copy key uses abspath, but render saves under the resolved path, so the rewrite check can silently turn off.
why: check_document(path) reads the copy under abspath(path) (line 220); _render saves under abspath(Path(path).resolve()) (lines 201, 226). If the path crosses a junction, symlink, subst drive or 8.3 name the keys differ: check reports saved_copy 'none' and a rewritten settled round passes. Inferred from the code; not run on such a path.
fix: Resolve the path inside _copy_path so every verb uses one key.
evidence: key = os.path.normcase(os.path.abspath(document)).encode("utf-8")  vs  document = Path(path).resolve()

finding: A saved copy outlives its document and has no identity check, so a restored or recreated document at the same path is refused with no way out.
why: The copy is keyed by path only and lives outside git. Delete and recreate pages/grill-s1.json, or check out an older commit of it, and check says 'settled round N was removed' or 'never rewritten'; the only remedy is deleting a file in the data folder, which no message names.
fix: Store session id and started in the copy and ignore a copy whose identity differs; name the copy path in the refusal.
evidence: check_rewrite: found.append((("rounds",), f"settled round {n} was removed; a settled round is never rewritten"))

finding: The duplicate-session glob matches other sessions whose id ends with this id.
why: Session id may hold '-'. Document grill-x-s1.json (id x-s1) matches the pattern *-s1.json built for id s1, so rendering session s1 is refused as duplicate-session although no id is shared (ids 2026-10-30 and 30 fail the same way).
fix: List the pages folder and compare each name with <skill>-<id>.json for the 3 known skills.
evidence: for other in document.parent.glob(f"*-{session['id']}.json"):

finding: Only Refusal is caught, so an OSError or KeyError in render or in the saved copy gives a traceback, not one JSON object.
why: write_if_changed(html_path) raises OSError on a locked or read-only target (line 225); save_settled_copy (line 165) the same; read_saved_copy line 157 raises KeyError/TypeError for a copy that is valid JSON without a rounds object. main() (line 303) has no other handler, so the caller gets no JSON answer (contract: exit 2 for unreadable).
fix: Wrap the write and read steps and raise Refusal('unreadable', ...); or add a last-resort handler in main().
evidence: except Refusal as refusal: answer = {"ok": False, ...}  (engine.py main); return {int(n): text for n, text in saved["rounds"].items()}

criterion: Acceptance: one JSON object per verb, exit 0/1/2
finding: main() catches only Refusal; any other exception ends in a traceback with no JSON object.
why: Acceptance bullet 1 and SDD section 3 say every verb answers one JSON object with exit 0, 1 or 2; the callers (page_round.py, 0005) parse stdout as JSON.
fix: Catch OSError, KeyError, TypeError and SchemaError in main(), and answer them as `unreadable` (exit 2) or a named refusal.
evidence: `except Refusal as refusal:` is the only handler in main(). Unguarded sites: `{int(n): text for n, text in saved["rounds"].items()}` (engine.py:157, valid JSON without `rounds` raises KeyError; only `{broken` is tested) and `inject.write_if_changed(html_path, ...)` (engine.py:225, os.replace at inject.py:174 can raise PermissionError on Windows when the host holds the page). Reachability of the Windows case is inferred, not run.

finding: Possible loss of prompt boundaries: poll joins several host prompts into one `raw` string with a line break.
why: The acceptance bullet asks for the host's raw composed response verbatim; with 2+ prompts the engine invents the join, so a later parser cannot tell a prompt boundary from a line inside a note, and the S2 caller reads only `raw` (page_round.py wait, `answer.get("raw")`) and the Stop hook returns only `raw`.
fix: Return one prompt as `raw` and refuse or flag several, or keep the join but document it in the engine docstring and have ingest read `prompts`.
evidence:
"raw": "
".join(str(p.get("prompt", "")) for p in parsed.get("prompts", [])),  # test_poll_joins_several_prompts_with_one_line_break

finding: Item id allows spaces and '|', but the response grammar splits a line on spaces.
why: A card with id 'i a' produces the line 'i a accept | note'; ingest cannot tell id from token (D-32 grammar '<id> <token> | <note>'). The id also goes into a DOM id and a note id N-<round>-<id>. Session id has a pattern; item id has only minLength. The ingest split rule is inferred from D-32; the parser is not in this slice.
fix: Give item id and component id the same pattern as session id.
evidence: "id": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1}  /  runtime.js:133 lines.push(n ? id + ' ' + c + ' | ' + n : id + ' ' + c)

finding: The tooltip wrapper replaces text inside SVG text elements with HTML span elements.
why: wrap() skips script, style, textarea and the tip UI, not svg. A freestyle SVG text element holding a dictionary term gets an HTML span child; HTML elements inside SVG outside foreignObject are not rendered (inferred from SVG rules; not run), so the label disappears.
fix: Add 'svg' to the closest() exclusion list.
evidence: p.closest('script,style,noscript,textarea,.afkv2-tip,#afkv2-tip-box,#afkv2-nav,#afkv2-jump')

finding: The Stop hook as Codex runs it (stdin, stdout, exit 0) is tested only with no record; the never-fail-the-stop path is unexercised
why: Every with-record test calls codex_stop.main in-process with wait_for_answer patched; the __main__ block, including the except Exception branch that returns a systemMessage, runs only in the live test, skipped in CI. A record plus a PATH with no lavish-axi would reach the fallback in a cheap subprocess test.
fix: Add a subprocess test: write a record, run the hook with no lavish-axi on PATH, assert exit 0 and a systemMessage that names the fallback.
evidence: run_stop_hook with a record appears only at test line 1157 (inside the skipped live test); the test at line 1003 patches codex_stop.wait_for_answer

criterion: blast radius of a changed shared file
finding: Possible cost on every Codex turn end: the new Stop entry starts bare `python` even when no page waits.
why: The Stop hook fires on every Codex Stop of every developer who enables the plugin; the other two afkv2 hooks use .cmd (ADR-0005: .cmd 35 ms, Python 60 ms), and this one depends on `python` being on PATH; how Codex reports a missing or Store-stub `python` is unverified.
fix: Start a .cmd stub that exits 0 unless a page-waiting-<session>.json exists, and have it start codex_stop.py only then; or record the setup-chosen Python path.
evidence: "commandWindows": "python \"%PLUGIN_ROOT%\hooks\codex_stop.py\"" ; session-start.cmd and subagent-start.cmd are the .cmd pattern; ADR-0005 'Python hook ... slower start for every session and subagent'; D-34 does not weigh a .cmd pre-check.

finding: test registers the type name "map", which slice 0004 owns
why: Slice 0004 adds afkv2/engine/components/diagram_map.py (CMP-3 map), so scratch_type("map") raises ValueError (duplicate type) once 0004 lands (inferred: the registered name "map" is not read in 0004 code, it does not exist yet).
fix: Use a scratch name no real component can take, for example "scratch-map", in the registration and the document.
evidence: scratch_type("map") ... doc["maps"] = [{"type": "map", ...}]; 0004 contract line 36: afkv2/engine/components/diagram_map.py#def render_map ( CMP-3 )

finding: Map node validation has one valid example and no refusal case
why: engine.py:129-140 (_map_node) adds a range comparison 1 <= round_ <= last_round, required id and state, and node-id uniqueness; no test feeds a bad node, so each check can break unseen.
fix: Add cases: node round 0, last+1, bool, missing state, non-object node, duplicate node id; assert the named field.
evidence: the only map in the file is {"id": "n-1", "state": "open", "round": 1, "label": "x"} (line 583); a search for the word nodes in the test file finds no other site

finding: Browser draft behaviour is tested by string search in runtime.js, not by running it
why: The test passes while the draft code is dead or wrong, and fails on a harmless rename or reorder. The live test is skipped in CI, so no CI test runs draft save, restore or clear.
fix: Run runtime.js in a DOM (or in the live Edge test) and assert restore after reload and clear after send; or drop the source-text asserts.
evidence: assert runtime.index("sendQueuedPrompts();") < runtime.index("clearDraft();", ...); assert "location.pathname" not in runtime

finding: Launcher grammar has no negative case for extra or conflicting open flags, or for poll and end argument counts
why: launcher.py:77 is the allow-list that keeps host flags out; a change that widens it (any -- flag, or both --no-open and --reopen) passes every listed case.
fix: Add to the refusal list: open p.html --no-open --reopen, open p.html --share, end p.html extra, poll p.html --timeout-ms.
evidence: argv list has ["open"], ["open", "p.txt"], ["open", "missing.html"] but no open p.html with an extra flag; code: rest[1:] not in ([], ["--no-open"], ["--reopen"])

finding: Codex waiting-record clearing by a foreground poll is tested for feedback only
why: engine.py:276 clears the record only for feedback and ended; no test shows that a waiting or browser_disconnected poll keeps the record, or that ended clears it, so a change to clear on every status passes and would drop the Stop-hook wait.
fix: Add cases per host status (waiting and browser_disconnected keep; ended clears) with the host-poll-*.txt fixtures.
evidence: test_a_foreground_poll_on_codex_clears_the_record uses the default feedback fixture; code: if status in ("feedback", "ended") and thread: launcher.clear_waiting_record(...)

finding: No test pins the 5-second retry sleep for non-waiting statuses in the Stop-hook wait
why: The scripted poll advances the clock by itself, so deleting sleep(RETRY_SECONDS) (codex_stop.py:45-46) leaves every wait test green, yet a host that answers "error" at once would then cause a busy loop for up to 3600 s.
fix: Pass a recording sleep and assert it runs after error and browser_disconnected, and not after waiting.
evidence: test_the_wait_goes_on_past_waiting_and_a_closed_browser asserts only the result and len(poll.seen) == 5; code: if status != "waiting": sleep(RETRY_SECONDS)

finding: The only test of the real host and of the Windows .cmd job binding is skipped in CI
why: CI runs pytest afkv2/tests -q -rs with AFKV2_TEST_LAVISH_DIR unset (a search of .github finds no such variable), so start_batch and the kill-on-close job (launcher.py:217) have no CI test (test_exit_69 mocks start_batch), and the host-*.txt fixtures are the only CI proof of the 0.1.80 output shape; whether the fixtures were captured from 0.1.80 is unverified.
fix: Record the capture command and host version beside the fixtures, and add a Windows-only test that runs start_batch on a trivial .cmd and asserts the child dies with the job.
evidence: @pytest.mark.skipif(not LIVE, reason="AFKV2_TEST_LAVISH_DIR is not set"); tests.yml: afk-python -m pytest afkv2/tests -q -rs; test line 809: monkeypatch.setattr(launcher, "start_batch", unbound)

criterion: Acceptance: a round chip marks every item that needs the human in that round
finding: A blocked card gets the round chip, though it takes no mark and is not flagged as required.
why: PRD AC-034 limits the chip to items that need the human in that round; a blocked point waits on another open point (SDD section 6), and the same file sets `data-afkv2-required` only for state `open`.
fix: Chip only state `open` (the state that sets `data-afkv2-required`), or record why a blocked point needs the human; change test_a_blocked_card_takes_a_note_and_no_mark to match.
evidence: base_card.py:79 `if current and item["kind"] != "info" and state in ("open", "blocked"):`; test asserts `holds(html, "<textarea", "afkv2-round-chip")` for a blocked card. Reading of AC-034 is a judgment call.

finding: Success answers carry fields (`saved_copy`, `url`, `status`, `waiting_record`, `prompts`, `session_ended`) that no doc or caller names.
why: The module docstring documents the envelope only; the S2 caller reads `page` and `raw`, so the extra fields are surface a later change must keep or break.
fix: Document each verb's success fields in the engine docstring or drop the ones with no reader.
evidence: return {"ok": True, "verb": "show", "page": str(html_path), "url": session.get("url"), "status": ..., "waiting_record": record}

finding: `show --no-open` and `--reopen` have no consumer outside the tests.
why: SDD section 3 lists the page document path as the only show input; the S2 caller (origin/feat/afkv2-s2 page_round.py present) calls show with no flag, and I found no other call in afkv2/ or docs (rg for reopen|no-open).
fix: Drop both flags until a caller names one, or name the consumer in the engine docstring.
evidence: mode.add_argument("--no-open", action="store_true"); mode.add_argument("--reopen", action="store_true")

finding: Host stderr goes to DEVNULL, so a node crash gives an empty reason.
why: A host that fails before it prints TOON (missing module, syntax error) writes to stderr only; poll_status then returns status 'error' with an empty reason and engine reports 'item page, field host: exit 1: ' with no cause.
fix: Capture stderr to a second temp file and append it to the reason when the exit code is not 0.
evidence: _spawn(command, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=out, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)

finding: A note whose target is a map node cannot settle a card, though SDD lets a note target any element id.
why: live drops every note with n['target'] in nodes. A settled_by_note item whose signal is a live note on its map node is refused with 'must be the id of a live note on this item'. SDD section 4: 'target = any element id'. Intent unverified.
fix: Drop the target filter, or record the rule in a decision and word the refusal to match.
evidence: live = {n["id"] for n in notes if not n["deleted"] and n["target"] not in nodes}

finding: A schema with additionalProperties set to a schema object is accepted by check_schema but never applied.
why: KEYWORDS lists additionalProperties and the module docstring says a keyword is never ignored in silence, but line 98 acts only on the value False; a component registering an additionalProperties schema gets no check on extra keys.
fix: Reject non-boolean additionalProperties in check_schema, or validate extra keys against it.
evidence: elif schema.get("additionalProperties") is False:

finding: Possible tight retry: a `browser_disconnected` poll answer is retried every 5 s for up to an hour.
why: Host poll returns at once when every window is disconnected past the grace period (dist/cli.mjs line 12521 text), so the hook may start about 720 host processes while the person is away (unverified: not run).
fix: Back off on browser_disconnected, or end the wait with the fallback message after a few repeats.
evidence: if status != "waiting": sleep(RETRY_SECONDS)

finding: A loop with an if verb == "poll" branch steers setup inside one test body
why: One test covers two verbs with different setup; a failure does not say which verb broke.
fix: Parametrize over the verb and prepare the page file in a fixture.
evidence: for verb in ("show", "poll"): if verb == "poll": path.with_suffix(".html").write_text(...)

finding: Hook timeout test hard-codes 3600 instead of tying to codex_stop.WAIT_SECONDS
why: D-34 says to change timeout_s and the hooks.json timeout together; if WAIT_SECONDS grows past 3610 the test stays green while the harness cuts the wait.
fix: Assert entry["timeout"] > codex_stop.WAIT_SECONDS.
evidence: assert "codex_stop.py" in entry["commandWindows"] and entry["timeout"] > 3600

criterion: changed paths match a ## Scope glob
finding: Pre-existing live-check file is edited but no ## Scope glob of 0003 names it.
why: The contract Scope lists 14 paths and none matches afkv2/tests/live/*; Acceptance requires the check there, so the contract is inconsistent with itself. D-35 records the exception but the contract is not amended.
fix: Add afkv2/tests/live/CODEX-LIVE-CHECKS.md to the 0003 ## Scope in the same change as D-35.
evidence: Scope: afkv2/hooks/hooks.json, afkv2/tests/engine/test_engine_core.py, afkv2/tests/engine/fixtures/* (no tests/live). Acceptance: 'is an owner-run step in afkv2/tests/live/CODEX-LIVE-CHECKS.md'. D-35: 'is outside the Scope globs, but the contract Acceptance and the brief name it'.
